item.description: SKハイニックス米公募価格149ドル、米イラン応酬、マイクロン投資増額、NY連銀総裁、メタが課金制

item.title: Why Young Investors Are Betting It All
item.description: Faced with rising expenses, massive student debt and diminishing job prospects, throwing the dice is looking increasingly attractive to some.

item.title: Secretive China Chipmaker Is Built to Dodge US Curbs
item.description: Founded by a US-trained entrepreneur, CXMT is racing to catch its rivals and using a largely domestic supplier network to shield itself from Washington.

item.title: South Korea Eyes AI Windfall Fund to Aid Growth, Jobs for Youth
item.description: South Korea plans to use part of an expected tax windfall from its booming chip sector to support young people, its labor minister said, as surging AI-related demand boosts the economy for now while fueling concerns over a wave of job cuts to come.

item.title: SK Hynix Is Said to Price US Share Offering at $149 Apiece
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. priced its US listing of American depositary receipts at $149 each, according to a person familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified as the information isn’t public.

item.title: Polymarket Seeks License to Offer Margin Trading Legally in US
item.description: Polymarket is seeking regulatory approval to offer margin trading in the US, a move that would let users bet on events with less capital upfront and help the prediction market platform attract more sophisticated traders.

item.title: Lutnick Presses SK Hynix, Samsung to Boost Memory Output in US
item.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick called on Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. to step up their efforts to expand memory chip production in the US to help address a global shortage in components critical to the development of artificial intelligence.

item.title: It’s Not Just Open Source Models Competing on Price
item.description: Cheap closed source models exist too.

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic Hit New Speed Bump With US Government
item.description: The Trump administration is taking a more active role in reviewing AI models.

item.title: Is SpaceX a Value Stock? Fidelity and FTSE Russell Think So
item.description: SpaceX has made its way into several value-oriented indexes

item.title: SK Hynix’s $26.5 Billion Listing Reopens Asia Route to US Market
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s US share sale is set to boost an ailing vehicle that was once essential for Asian firms looking West, and Wall Street is hoping the frenzy for artificial intelligence infrastructure will encourage competitors to follow their path.

item.title: Fed’s Warsh Names Leadership for Five New Task Forces
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh announced the leadership of five task forces that will examine the central bank’s approach to key aspects of policy making, with an eye toward potentially enacting sweeping changes.

item.title: Lagarde Says She’s Not a Candidate for French Election: Euronews
item.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said she’ll try to have her voice heard during next year’s French presidential election, while declining that she’s pondering a campaign herself.

item.title: Goldman Bans Staff Prediction Markets Bets on Finance, Politics
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. has banned employees from trading on prediction markets except for sports and entertainment bets, in one of the most pointed efforts by a Wall Street firm grappling with the new regulatory issues raised by the boom in betting on events.

item.title: UPS, FedEx Shares Fall on Growing Threat From Amazon Shipping
item.description: United Parcel Service Inc. and FedEx Corp. shares tumbled after an analyst warned that Amazon.com Inc. is offering inexpensive and increasingly fast delivery services to third-party customers, underscoring the risk posed by the e-commerce giant to traditional shipping firms.

item.title: End of an Era: Longtime Podcast Hosts Go Quiet as Video Dominates
item.description: Veteran hosts like Marc Maron, Al Franken and the Culture Gabfest crew are hanging up their headphones and setting down their mics.

item.title: Wayve Staff Sold Stock at 10% Discount on LSE’s Pisces Exchange
item.description: Wayve Technologies Ltd. employees sold shares on London’s new private market at a 10% discount to the self-driving technology startup’s previous valuation, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Kimmeridge Faults Pace of Devon Energy’s Asset-Sale Efforts
item.description: Kimmeridge Energy Management Co., an outspoken shale investor, criticized Devon Energy Corp.’s divestment program as too slow after the driller’s $25 billion takeover of Coterra Energy Inc.

item.title: Meta’s Zuckerberg Says Exploring AI Cloud Business Makes Sense
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. needs all the computing power it can get, Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg said, but in a market starved for resources necessary to run and develop artificial intelligence products he’s also considering whether some of Meta’s AI infrastructure could be more valuable if rented to outsiders.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar Surges as Economic Data Fuels Rate Hike Bets
item.description: The New Zealand dollar advanced Thursday to the highest in more than two weeks after strong manufacturing data increased bets on further monetary tightening in the nation.

item.title: France Seen Dodging Recession as Central Bank Lifts GDP Estimate
item.description: The Bank of France raised its short-term growth estimate as activity improved in all sectors in June, indicating the economy will safely avoid a recession.

item.title: Oil Industry Retained Up to €200 Million of German Fuel Subsidy
item.description: Germany’s oil industry retained between €100 million and €200 million from a fuel tax reduction earlier this year that was intended to ease the impact of surging costs on motorists, a government advisory panel found.

item.title: Spain’s Joint Debt Proposal Questioned by EU’s Largest Economies
item.description: A Spanish bid to boost joint debt issuance by the European Union was met with skepticism from some of the bloc’s top economies.

item.title: Franklin’s Dudley Sees AI Infrastructure Bull Case Through 2027
item.description: Franklin Templeton’s Katrina Dudley said the bull case for infrastructure spending on artificial intelligence is winning out over bear arguments and sees the investment theme remaining durable through 2027 and potentially into the year beyond.

item.title: OpenAI Unveils ChatGPT Work Agent to Field Tasks for Hours
item.description: OpenAI is introducing a new artificial intelligence agent that’s meant to field a wider range of complex tasks for hours at a time, bolstering its push to appeal to more business professionals.

item.title: ING Weighs Venezuela Commodity Deals as Client Requests Rise
item.description: ING Groep, one of the top financiers of commodity trading, is fielding “a lot” of calls from clients to support Venezuelan natural resource deals as the country revamps exports after years of US sanctions, its new Americas commodity finance head said.

item.title: KPMG UK to Slash 200 Back Office Roles in Latest Round of Cuts
item.description: KPMG UK is cutting 10% of staff across its support teams, according to a spokesperson for the company, in the latest round of job cuts by the Big Four accountancy firm.

item.title: Wall Street Finds a New Way to Help Investors Avoid Elon Musk
item.description: For every investor who wants more Elon Musk, Wall Street increasingly has an ETF. Now it’s planning some for investors who want less.

item.title: Former Fed Chairman Ben Bernanke Joins Anthropic Oversight Trust
item.description: Former Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke has been appointed to Anthropic’s long-term benefit trust, an oversight body meant to keep the artificial intelligence company accountable to its public mission.

item.title: UK Fintech Lendable Pledges Personal Loans to Raise £500 Million
item.description: UK digital lender Lendable Ltd. is raising £500 million ($671 million) by selling securities backed by a portfolio of personal loans, a deal that would support its ambitions to push further into lending.
